koota_varna_explanation: Varna compares traditional classifications of the Moon signs. This baseline applies the conventional groom-equal-or-higher rule; it is a traditional scoring convention, not a measure of personal worth.
koota_vashya_explanation: Vashya compares traditional sign groups associated with mutual influence. Sign groups are used as a baseline; regional tables and boundary conventions can differ.
koota_tara_explanation: Tara evaluates the distance between the two birth Nakshatras in both directions. Sampat, Kshema, Sadhaka, Mitra and Parama Mitra are treated as favorable in this scoring convention.
koota_yoni_explanation: Yoni compares traditional animal symbols assigned to Nakshatras. This baseline awards full points for the same animal, zero for listed enemy pairs and partial points otherwise; regional tables may differ.
koota_graha_maitri_explanation: Graha Maitri compares natural friendship between lords of the two Moon signs. This baseline does not include temporary planetary relationships from full birth charts.
koota_gana_explanation: Gana compares traditional temperament groups of the birth Nakshatras: Deva, Manushya and Rakshasa. This is a commonly used baseline; some traditions apply gender-sensitive variations.
koota_bhakoot_explanation: Bhakoot compares the Moon-sign distance. Conventional 2/12, 5/9 and 6/8 relationships receive zero points in this baseline. Cancellation rules and regional interpretations are not evaluated.
koota_nadi_explanation: Nadi compares Adi, Madhya and Antya classifications assigned to Nakshatras. This score does not apply Nadi Dosha cancellation rules or exceptions, which require additional traditional checks.

birth_boundary_disclaimer: This birth time is very close to a Nakshatra/Pada boundary. Small differences in ephemeris or recorded birth time may change the result. Please verify with a professional Panchang or ephemeris.
birth_calculation_disclaimer: Astrology is a traditional belief system. The calculation uses a geocentric lunar model and an approximate Lahiri ayanamsha; boundary cases should be cross-checked.
kundali_accuracy_disclaimer: Planet positions use GeoEngine with the app’s approximate Lahiri ayanamsha. D1 uses whole-sign houses; Bhava Chalit uses calculated quadrant-based Bhava Madhya and Sandhi boundaries. Validate important readings against a trusted ephemeris; this is not a Swiss Ephemeris-validated chart.
muhurat_not_ready: Exact auspicious time windows are not shown yet. They require a verified location-based Panchang calculation using Tithi, Nakshatra, Yoga, Karana, weekday and relevant dosha periods. No time has been assumed or generated.

graha_motion_note: Daily motion is estimated from positions around the birth time. Rahu and Ketu use the mean-node model. The underlying planetary and ayanamsha model is approximate and should be checked against a trusted ephemeris for precision work.

dasha_calculation_note: Vimshottari uses the Moon's birth Nakshatra lord and a 120-year cycle. The remaining first Mahadasha is proportional to the untraversed part of the Nakshatra; Antardasha lengths are proportional to their planetary year allocations. Dates use 365.2425 days per Dasha year. Traditional interpretations are not guaranteed predictions.

varga_accuracy_note: Divisional charts are derived from the natal sidereal longitudes using traditional Parashari sign-division rules. Small birth-time or ephemeris errors can change divisional placements, especially in higher Vargas. These charts show placements only; interpretations require additional factors and should not be treated as certain predictions.

graha_education_disclaimer: This page presents traditional Jyotish and cultural associations for general learning. Interpretations vary by lineage. Gemstones and mantras are traditional practices, not guaranteed remedies or medical, financial or personal advice. Rahu and Ketu are lunar nodes, not physical planets.
graha_sun_summary: Surya represents vitality, self-expression, authority and the principle of illumination in Jyotish.
graha_sun_nature: The Sun is traditionally treated as a royal, authoritative and naturally intense Graha. It is associated with clarity, leadership, dignity and independence.
graha_sun_karaka: Soul (Atman), father, authority, government, leadership, reputation, confidence, vitality and the capacity to take responsibility.
graha_sun_qualities: Clarity, courage, integrity, self-respect, generosity, leadership and a strong sense of purpose.
graha_sun_body: Traditionally associated with the heart, bones, eyes (especially the right eye in some texts), head and general vitality.
graha_moon_summary: Chandra represents the mind, emotions, nourishment, receptivity and the rhythms of everyday life.
graha_moon_nature: The Moon is receptive, nurturing and changeable. Its traditional benefic or challenging character is also considered in relation to its waxing or waning phase.
graha_moon_karaka: Mind (Manas), mother, emotions, public life, comfort, nourishment, fluids, home, memory and mental ease.
graha_moon_qualities: Empathy, adaptability, care, imagination, receptivity, emotional awareness and the ability to nurture.
graha_moon_body: Traditionally associated with the mind, fluids, chest, breasts, stomach and the body's rhythms.
graha_mars_summary: Mangala represents energy, courage, initiative, competition and the drive to act.
graha_mars_nature: Mars is traditionally fiery, active, decisive and forceful. It signifies the capacity to confront obstacles and protect boundaries.
graha_mars_karaka: Courage, younger siblings, physical energy, initiative, land, property, tools, technical skill, conflict and disciplined action.
graha_mars_qualities: Courage, decisiveness, endurance, initiative, strategic action, protection and the ability to work under pressure.
graha_mars_body: Traditionally associated with blood, muscles, bone marrow, heat, injuries and physical drive.
graha_mercury_summary: Budha represents intellect, communication, learning, calculation, trade and practical reasoning.
graha_mercury_nature: Mercury is considered adaptable and analytical. Classical Jyotish often describes it as impressionable, taking on qualities from the Grahas it associates with.
graha_mercury_karaka: Intellect, speech, writing, mathematics, education, commerce, negotiation, humour, friends and analytical skills.
graha_mercury_qualities: Curiosity, clear communication, logic, versatility, wit, observation and the ability to connect ideas.
graha_mercury_body: Traditionally associated with the nervous system, skin, speech, respiratory pathways and coordination.
graha_jupiter_summary: Guru represents wisdom, knowledge, ethics, guidance, expansion and the search for meaning.
graha_jupiter_nature: Jupiter is traditionally considered a great natural benefic, associated with generosity, growth, faith, learning and wise counsel.
graha_jupiter_karaka: Teachers, guides, children, higher learning, sacred knowledge, dharma, ethics, prosperity, faith and good counsel.
graha_jupiter_qualities: Wisdom, optimism, generosity, patience, fairness, broad understanding and the ability to guide others.
graha_jupiter_body: Traditionally associated with the liver, fat, growth, metabolism and the body's nourishing processes.
graha_venus_summary: Shukra represents relationships, beauty, enjoyment, refinement, art and the capacity to appreciate life.
graha_venus_nature: Venus is traditionally a gentle benefic associated with harmony, attraction, pleasure, refinement and the arts.
graha_venus_karaka: Marriage and partnership, love, spouse, beauty, music, art, vehicles, comforts, luxuries and material enjoyment.
graha_venus_qualities: Affection, diplomacy, creativity, appreciation of beauty, harmony, charm and the ability to build relationships.
graha_venus_body: Traditionally associated with reproductive vitality, kidneys, complexion, and the body's reproductive and restorative systems.
graha_saturn_summary: Shani represents time, responsibility, discipline, endurance, service and the results of sustained effort.
graha_saturn_nature: Saturn is traditionally slow, serious, dry and disciplined. It is associated with limits, patience, labour, accountability and maturity.
graha_saturn_karaka: Work, service, labourers, longevity, delay, discipline, hardship, responsibility, old age, humility and perseverance.
graha_saturn_qualities: Patience, persistence, realism, reliability, restraint, humility and the ability to build lasting foundations.
graha_saturn_body: Traditionally associated with bones, teeth, joints, knees, nerves and chronic or long-lasting conditions; this is not medical guidance.
graha_rahu_summary: Rahu is the north lunar node, associated in Jyotish with ambition, appetite, unconventional paths and amplification.
graha_rahu_nature: Rahu is a shadow Graha rather than a physical planet. It is commonly described as intense, worldly, disruptive, ambitious and boundary-crossing.
graha_rahu_karaka: Ambition, worldly desire, foreign places, innovation, unconventional subjects, mass influence, obsession, smoke and sudden change.
graha_rahu_qualities: Original thinking, ambition, adaptability to unfamiliar environments, experimentation and the drive to explore new possibilities.
graha_rahu_body: Some traditions associate Rahu with the head, skin, toxins and unusual or difficult-to-classify conditions. This is symbolic, not medical advice.
graha_ketu_summary: Ketu is the south lunar node, associated with detachment, inward insight, release and spiritual investigation.
graha_ketu_nature: Ketu is a shadow Graha rather than a physical planet. It is traditionally linked with separation, inward focus, subtle perception and liberation.
graha_ketu_karaka: Detachment, moksha, spiritual practice, intuition, renunciation, past impressions, research, mysteries and sudden separation.
graha_ketu_qualities: Insight, introspection, discernment, simplicity, spiritual curiosity, independence and the ability to let go.
graha_ketu_body: Some traditions associate Ketu with the feet, nervous sensitivity and subtle or hard-to-classify conditions. This is symbolic, not medical advice.
